title: Compact support and coefficient extension retain the finite-Tor domain
statement: Fix a field $k$ of characteristic $p>0$ and a prime $\ell\ne p$. Let $h:U\to V$ be a separated finite-type map of separated finite-type $k$-schemes, with compactification $U\xrightarrow jW\xrightarrow rV$ in the same class [sk-def-sfb-dc-setting]. Let $A\to B$ be a unital map of finite commutative rings killed by powers of $\ell$. Use the ordinary constant-ring module derived categories [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories] [def-weil-pbc-proetale-modules]. Write $N_T=\nu_T^*$ for site pullback [def-weil-pbc-site-comparison-morphism] and $E_B=E\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}B$ for coefficient extension on either site [det-sp-scalar-extension-functor] [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings]. Let $L\in D^b(U_{\rm et},A)$ have constructible cohomology and finite Tor amplitude, meaning a uniform finite cohomology interval for its tensor with each degree-zero module sheaf [def-weil-pbc-etale-constructible-sheaf] [def-kun-tor-amplitude]. Put $F_R^{\rm et}=Rr_{*,R}^{\rm et}j_{!,R}^{\rm et}$ and $F_R^{\rm pro}=Rr_{*,R}^{\rm pro}j_{!,R}^{\rm pro}$ [def-amb-etale-compact-support] [det-sp-reduction-direct-image]. Then $F_A^{\rm et}L$ and $F_B^{\rm et}(L_B)$ are bounded constructible of finite Tor amplitude, and so are their site pullbacks, with intrinsically constructible cohomology and finite Tor amplitude on the pro-etale site [def-weil-proetale-constructible-sheaf] [def-weil-proetale-tor-amplitude]. The complexes $(F_A^{\rm et}L)_B$ and $L_B$ are bounded constructible of finite Tor amplitude as well. The specified map $N_VF_R^{\rm et}E\to F_R^{\rm pro}N_UE$ obtained by the proper counit mate and the open comparison is an isomorphism for every bounded-below etale input $E$ [lem-weil-pbc-comparison-direct-image-canonical-mate] [lem-cbc-proetale-extension-zero-comparison]. Consequently all these inputs and actual scalar extensions lie in $D^+$; no finite projective dimension of $B/A$ is assumed. Schemes and Noetherian rings use [def-pc-scheme] [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring].

proof.text: Finite type over Spec k gives compactness and local Noetherianity of U and V, hence IsNoetherian. The over relation identifies h followed by the structure map with the structure map of U, so h is quasi-compact. If R is killed by ell^n, then (ell^n : R)=0 by evaluation at 1. Since ell is prime and differs from char k, ell is nonzero in k. Its nth power is a unit in k and hence in the global sections of Spec k and V. Thus R has invertible exponent on V. This includes the zero ring and empty schemes.

Use the proved ordinary etale specialization of single-compactification preservation, rightDerivedLowerShriekOfCompactification_isTriangulated_and_ctf, at the given c. Translate intrinsic constructibility with isConstructibleEtaleModuleSheaf_iff_isConstructibleSheaf and translate Tor intervals with hasTorAmplitudeIn_iff_torAmplitudeIn. This proves Dctf preservation for this exact c without passing through condensed internal modules.

proof.text: For any Dctf etale K on a Noetherian T, widen an unordered Tor witness [a,b] to [min(a,b),b]. Apply finiteCoefficientInputModels to K and A -> B. Its clauses give bounded intrinsic constructible site pullback, its Tor interval, bounded constructible actual etale scalar extension with that interval, and bounded actual proetale scalar extension. Apply the same theorem with B -> B the identity to obtain the site-pullback properties of each B-output. Bounds in the two constructibility presentations translate using isGE_iff and isLE_iff.

proof.text: Apply compact-support preservation to L over A; scalar preservation to L and F_A L; compact-support preservation to L_B over B. These give all four etale outputs and their intrinsic site pullbacks. A bounded complex has a lower bound. Exact proetale open extension and left t-exact right-derived direct image carry the lower bound to both actual proetale compact-support outputs. The scalar clauses supply lower bounds for the two actual proetale scalar outputs. Resolve the finite list memberships to assemble the conclusion.

proof.text: For the second declaration, the proper map c.g is qcqs. isIso_fixedComparisonDirectImageMatePlus makes its actual named counit mate invertible. The derived open comparison is the component of a composite natural isomorphism. Its right-derived direct image is invertible, and so is the composite. This uses precisely the two arrows displayed in the unchanged theorem statement.
